flawed_step: The proof would need to infer Hall's condition |N(S)| >= |S| for every S subseteq A. The degree assumptions only imply |S| <= 2|N(S)|, which does not justify Hall's condition.
counterexample: Let A={a1,a2}, B={b}, and E={a1b,a2b}. Each vertex of A has degree 1 and b has degree 2, but no matching saturates both vertices of A.
assessment_summary: The statement is false: the degree bounds permit two vertices of A to have the same unique neighbor, preventing a matching that saturates A.
